title: Approvals & Merging
definition: The final steps of a Pull Request workflow where reviewers formally accept the changes, and the code is subsequently integrated into the base branch.
simpleExplanation: Once you fix all the things your reviewers pointed out, they click a button that says 'Approve' (which adds a big green checkmark to your PR). Once you have enough approvals, the 'Merge' button unlocks, and you can squash your code into the main branch.
realWorldExample: A company policy might require strictly 2 Approvals from Senior Developers before any code can be merged into the `production` branch.

basic: What are the three statuses a reviewer can submit?
intermediate: What is the difference between 'Create a merge commit' and 'Squash and merge'?

answers.question: Three statuses?
answers.answer: 1. Comment (Just leaving thoughts), 2. Approve (Looks good, ready to merge), 3. Request Changes (Forces the PR to remain blocked until specific fixes are made).

answers.question: Merge commit vs Squash?
answers.answer: 'Merge commit' takes all 50 of your tiny commits and dumps them into the main history timeline, plus adds a 51st commit tying them together. 'Squash and merge' crushes your 50 commits into 1 single clean commit and places it on the main timeline.
